claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 19 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 19 years old and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 19, I need to ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** 

(For example, is he in full-time non-advanced education, or on an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is in education. He's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know that Alex is studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

Just to confirm a couple more details:

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Just one more important question to complete my assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another relative?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually - Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him. They live with us too.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I'm afraid **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

Here's why:

While Alex meets the criteria (he's 19 and in approved education studying A-levels, which is allowed), and you live in the UK with responsibility for him, **only one person can get Child Benefit for any child**. Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you cannot also make a claim.

However, if circumstances change in the future - for example, if the other parent wanted to stop claiming and you wanted to claim instead - you would need to:
1. Have the current claimant contact the Child Benefit Office to explain they want to stop
2. Agree between yourselves who will claim
3. The new claimant would then need to make a new claim

If you and the other parent cannot agree on who should claim, HMRC would make the decision.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

However, according to the Child Benefit rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, the claimant cannot also claim Child Benefit for Alex. Two people cannot get Child Benefit for the same child.
